newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bank support cost seen at 8.5 pct '96 GDP.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bank support cost seen at 8.5 pct '96 GDP.

text.p: The total fiscal cost of Mexico's banking sector support programs is expected to reach 212.3 billion pesos in net present value, equivalent to 8.5 percent of 1996 estimated Gross Domestic Product (GDP), the Finance Ministry said in a report on Wednesday.

Of the total fiscal cost, some 30 percent will have already been financed by year-end 1997, the ministry said. The remainder, which amounts to 148.64 billion pesos, will be financed mainly by the banking system in the next 30 years, it added.

The ministry said the cost was estimated for the total life of the program, which was implemented in 1995, shortly after the peso crisis caused interest rates to skyrocket and customers to start defaulting on bank loans.

The ministry said the banking system's capitalization index has increased from 8 percent in February 1995 to 14.5 percent in October 1996, without taking into account capital commitments from purchased loans for the rest of the year.
It added provisions to past due loans for the system averaged 92 percent in October versus 45 percent in the beginning of 1995.
